newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: No broking firms suspended from trading - KLSE.
newsitem.headline: No broking firms suspended from trading - KLSE.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) has not suspended any stockbroking firms from trading, and no broker has defaulted on payment to the exchange's clearing house, the Star newspaper quoted the exchange as saying on Wednesday.
"The KLSE wishes to confirm that it has not suspended any stockbroking company," Nik Mohamed Din, KLSE executive chairman, was quoted as saying in a statement to the newspaper.
"We further wish to confirm that none of our stockbroking companies have defaulted on their payments to our clearing house," the statement said.
Stock exchange officials could not immediately be reached for comment on Wednesday.
The Malaysian stock market's slide in the past few weeks has prompted rumours about cash flow problems at several brokers and the suspension of dealers.

Talk circulated in the market on Tuesday that several firms had been suspended from trading for exceeding their lending limits. But fund managers and dealers told Reuters the speculation appeared unfounded as they had executed trades through the firms.

The Composite Index of blue chip stocks ended down 1.31 percent at 1,086.67 on Tuesday. Share prices have been in a downdraft ever since the announcement on March 28 of new restrictions on property and stock purchase lending.
